Here it is necessary that you follow me, not I you. And although you may still hurl more thunderbolts against me, my Monarchy shall nevertheless stand, while all of yours goes to ruin. I do not write so extensively about Alchemy in vain, but I do so with this intent and end: that from these things you may learn nearly and solidly what lies hidden within it, and how it ought to be understood. Nor should you be offended by the fact that neither gold nor silver comes forth from it. Rather, care must be taken that through it the <term>arcana</term> <gloss>secret healing powers</gloss> are uncovered, and the deceptions of the <term>seplasiarii</term> <gloss>perfumers or sellers of ointments</gloss> are exposed, by which the unrefined common folk are deceived, while these men serve them for one florin what they would not redeem for a single penny. So "precious" are their secrets.

<margin>Poison even in the best things.</margin>
Who is there who would dare to deny that poison lies hidden and remains even in the best of things? Everyone is compelled to confess this. If this is true, I now ask you: must the poison not be separated from the good and useful? And the good taken, the evil left behind? Indeed, it must be so. If therefore it is necessary, I pray you, tell me how that separation is performed in your workshops? For among you, everything remains mixed together. But so that you may protect your own simplicity, if you are forced to confess that poison lies hidden there, and are asked where it finally goes, you then bring forth I know not what regarding "corrections," which supposedly drive out and take away the poison, <margin>The "correction" of the Physicians is examined.</margin> just as they say Quince corrects Scammony <note>a harsh purgative resin</note>, or as they speak of <term>Diagridium</term> <gloss>scammony juice prepared with quince</gloss>. But what kind of correction is this? Does the poison not remain afterward just as it did at first? And yet you, meanwhile, boast that you have corrected it, so that the poison no longer harms. But where did it escape to? <margin>Diagridium.</margin> It remains in the <term>Diagridium</term>. Test it, if you are wise: exceed the proper limit, and you will see where the poison is. For you will find out soon enough. In this way you also correct <term>Turbith</term> <gloss>an East Indian root used as a purgative</gloss> and call it <term>Diaturbith</term>. Such are your corrections, which would be fitting for peasants and should be given to pack-horses. Make a trial by exceeding the measure and increasing the dose: you will see whether you do not feel the poison. <margin>What it means to "Correct."</margin> *To correct is to take what has been corrected.* If someone is malicious and has sinned, and he is punished, the correction does not extend further than the will of the one who was punished lasts. These corrections of yours are of such a kind; the power lies with the substances themselves, not with you. Now in this case, a Physician should consider nothing further than that the poison be removed. This must be done through separation. As for example: a serpent is poisonous, and yet it is adopted for food. If you remove the poison from it, you may eat it without harm. The same must be understood equally of all other things, namely that a similar separation is necessary. Until that is done, you cannot be secure in your operation, unless by chance it happens that nature supplies your deficiencies, or a greater kindness of the heavens favors you. For in your art, no protection remains.

Now therefore, if that true foundation which removes poison is required, let us see how Alchemy provides it. For it is necessary that it be done in such a way that, if <term>Mars</term> <gloss>iron or the martial quality</gloss> is in the <term>Sun</term> <gloss>gold or the solar quality</gloss>, Mars is removed; and if <term>Saturn</term> <gloss>lead or the saturnine quality</gloss> dwells in <term>Venus</term> <gloss>copper or the venereal quality</gloss>, it is separated from her. For as many as there are ascendants and impressions in the things of nature, so many bodies also exist within them. Truly, whichever bodies are contrary, it is entirely necessary that some of them be diminished and taken away, so that in this way all contrariety is removed, and the evil is taken from the good which you seek. <margin>Fire perfects all things.</margin> Just as gold is useful for nothing unless it is first cast into the fire, so a Medicine is much less useful which does not pass through the fire. For it is necessary for all things to pass through the fire into a second generation, by which they ought to benefit and help man. And should this not rightly be judged the honest foundation of any Physician? For a Physician ought not to employ poisons, but rather <term>arcana</term>. <margin>The pharmacies are rebuked.</margin> However, all those medicinal preparations, as many as they are, do not contribute even a single letter to this doctrine; they are simply occupied in "correcting," as if a dog has farted in a room and that stench is suppressed either by troches and incense, or by juniper wood. I ask you, does the stench not remain in the room afterward just as before? And although it is not perceived by the sense of smell, is it therefore permitted for anyone to say the stench has been separated and remains no longer? On the contrary, it is present, but "corrected" by the fumigation. Thus the fumigation and the foul air enter the nostrils together. Such also are the corrections of the Pharmacists, who blunt <term>Aleopaticum</term> <note>a bitter medicinal compound</note> with sugar, so that it inflicts no harm. Thus sugar and honey are their highest mastery. In this way they also correct gentian with theriac. Are these not the works of asinine ignorance? Yet they boast and sell themselves as the Physicians of princes. Who is so stupid as not to smell instantly that these things are worthless? What else, I ask, can they boast of regarding their remedies except to say: *This Electuary is sweet, made of spices and sugar,*

<summary>Paracelsus argues that true medicine requires the alchemical separation of poisons from healing substances rather than merely masking unpleasantness with sugar or incense. He critiques contemporary pharmacists for their superficial "corrections" of drugs like scammony and gentian, asserting that only fire and alchemical art can truly purify a remedy for human use.</summary>
<keywords>Alchemy, Pharmacy, Toxicology, Separation, Scammony, Mars, Saturn, Medical Ethics, Purgatives, Arcana</keywords>
